In a previously released joint status report, Apple stated that it is still awaiting additional documents from Jon Prosser and hopes to take another deposition from Michael Ramacciotti, while the two defendants object to the way Apple is handling the case. Details are as follows.

According to the joint status report submitted to Judge James Donato, Apple, leaker Jon Prosser, and Michael Ramacciotti are increasingly at odds over who should be held responsible for the delays in the case. This trade secrets lawsuit was filed by Apple against both defendants simultaneously in July 2025.

A little background

As a reminder, shortly after unveiling iOS 26, Apple filed a trade secrets misappropriation lawsuit against Prosser and Ramacciotti over Prosser's video, in which he leaked several elements of the system, including what turned out to be the major Liquid Glass visual redesign.

Apple alleges that Ramacciotti improperly accessed a development iPhone belonging to an employee, who was subsequently fired over the incident, and showed Prosser unreleased iOS features running on the device via a FaceTime call.

The case has since seen plenty of dramatic developments, including a default judgment entered by the court clerk because Prosser failed to respond to Apple's complaint within the deadline—though Prosser has disputed outside characterizations that he was ignoring the case.

Eight months later, the court agreed to vacate that default judgment, giving him another chance to formally answer the allegations.

Court filings show that Ramacciotti's side has responded to Apple's complaint and is largely cooperating with Apple's discovery requests.

However, since Prosser hired counsel and formally entered the case, the situation has taken a sharp turn for the worse, and the three sides have increasingly clashed over who should bear responsibility for the alleged trade secret disclosures and the resulting delays.

The new joint status report

Turning to the new status report, Apple says it wants Ramacciotti to update his interrogatory responses and sit for another deposition, to address what it claims are "inconsistencies between his testimony and Mr. Prosser's."

Ramacciotti, however, says he is willing to sit for another deposition as long as Apple provides "a roadmap for resolving the claims against him, including what additional information Apple needs from him (if anything)."

As for Prosser, Apple says it is "still awaiting certain additional documents it requested over three months ago," including revenue reports and analytics for his YouTube channel, as well as communications with third parties that he referenced during his deposition.

Prosser counters that "the trade secrets at issue no longer appear to be secret and have entered the public domain." In other words, his argument appears to be that since Apple has now released iOS updates featuring Liquid Glass, the information at the heart of the lawsuit is now public and no longer meets the definition of a trade secret.

As part of the joint status update, Ramacciotti has asked the court to hold a status conference this month, at which he wants Apple to specify what additional information it still needs from him. He also wants Apple to either drop the claims against him or commit to moving the case toward trial within 30 days thereafter.

Meanwhile, Apple wants discovery to continue, including a second deposition of Ramacciotti and production of the documents Prosser has yet to turn over. Prosser argues he has already fulfilled his agreed-upon discovery obligations and objects to Apple's continuing requests for more materials.

If Judge Donato does not grant Ramacciotti's request for a status conference, the parties suggest submitting another joint status report on December 2.
